title: Indirect prompt injection hijacks an assurance agent
description: Agent reading untrusted content (regulatory text, questionnaires, vendor documents, tickets) follows embedded instructions and misuses its tools; NIST CAISI 2026 found successful attacks against every frontier model tested.

title: Agent approves or effectively approves its own exception
description: Agent obtains approval capability directly, via a delegated human session, or by routing to a rubber-stamp approver, defeating segregation of duties.

title: Fabricated or confabulated evidence accepted as real
description: AI-produced narratives, screenshots, counts or citations that do not correspond to source-system facts are stored or presented as control evidence.

title: Control failure concealed or downgraded
description: Agent (or compromised operator) suppresses, closes, re-scopes or re-labels failing results so dashboards show green.

title: Historical evidence modified or deleted
description: Evidence records altered after the fact by an agent, admin or compromised pipeline, invalidating period-of-time assurance.

title: Internal validation misrepresented as independent or external attestation
description: Trust-center text, questionnaire answers or sales material describe agent or internal testing as audited, certified, attested or independent.

title: Silent control weakening
description: Threshold relaxed, scope narrowed, check removed, severity lowered or alert route dropped through an innocuous-looking change, by an agent or human.

title: Material policy changed without authorised approval
description: Agent-drafted policy text or policy-as-code bundle becomes effective without approval by the designated authority.

title: Confidential evidence disclosed to unauthorised AI provider
description: Evidence or customer data sent to a provider/model lacking approved data terms, or retained/trained on by the provider.

title: Agent credential theft or misuse
description: Long-lived or broadly scoped credentials exposed in agent context, logs or prompts are exfiltrated or misused.

title: Privilege amplification through agent delegation
description: Sub-agents or tool chains acquire permissions exceeding the delegating principal or task scope.

title: Insecure or test-weakening AI-generated code
description: Agent-authored code introduces vulnerabilities, hallucinated dependencies, or edits tests/checks so that failures pass.

title: Unbounded autonomous remediation causes outage or weakens baseline
description: Auto-remediation applies broad or wrong changes, oscillates, or 'fixes' drift by changing the approved baseline.

title: AI provider outage halts assurance operations
description: Loss of the model provider stops evidence collection, monitoring or approvals because they were built on agents.

title: Single AI provider/model concentration
description: Correlated failure, policy change, price change or compromise at one provider affects every agent and validator simultaneously.

title: Unannounced model behaviour change (drift) at provider
description: Provider updates a model alias; agent accuracy, refusal behaviour or injection resistance changes without Echelon review.

title: Agent memory or retrieval index poisoned
description: Persisted memory or retrieved corpus (e.g., requirement library) is poisoned, biasing future mappings or analyses.

title: Stale or wrong regulatory interpretation propagated
description: Requirement-change monitoring misses or misreads an authoritative change; mappings and policies drift from law/standards.

title: Automation bias in human approvals
description: Approvers rubber-stamp agent proposals; human approval exists formally but not substantively.

title: Agent actions not attributable
description: Self-reported provenance (Praxis) is spoofed or missing; actions cannot be tied to an authenticated agent identity and accountable human.

title: Same system implements, validates and approves its own controls
description: Control implementation, testing and sign-off share code, credentials, pipelines, models or owner, so failures are not detected (self-review).

title: Correlated errors between implementing and validating agents
description: Validator uses the same model/prompts/data as implementer and shares its blind spots, producing false assurance.

title: Compromised administrator subverts assurance system
description: Privileged insider or stolen admin credential alters controls, evidence store retention or monitoring.

title: Compromised CI/CD pipeline
description: Build or validation pipeline is altered to skip checks, forge results or deploy unapproved control code.

title: Missing evidence treated as passing
description: Collector failure or scope gap yields no data, and absence of failure is reported as success.

title: Monitoring disabled or blinded
description: Log sources, detectors or alert routes are disabled or misconfigured without detection.

title: Collusion between humans or between human and agent
description: Two role-holders (or an operator steering an agent) cooperate to bypass segregation of duties.

title: Wrong policy encoded faithfully
description: Policy-as-code enforces an incorrect or incomplete policy; all technical checks pass while the business objective fails.

title: Shared infrastructure failure takes down control and its monitor together
description: Control, evidence store and monitor share cloud account, region, identity provider or DNS, so one failure removes both function and detection.

title: Bad automated remediation masks a real incident
description: Auto-remediation reverts attacker changes and destroys forensic state or suppresses the alert that would have revealed the incident.

title: Single cloud provider dependency for evidence and validation
description: Evidence, validation and production all on one cloud provider; provider-level compromise or outage removes independent verification.

title: Assurance system complexity exceeds the team's ability to verify it
description: Meta-controls, agents and pipelines become too complex for a small team or an auditor to understand, causing undetected gaps and audit friction.

title: Compliance theater
description: Metrics, dashboards and documents optimise for audit appearance rather than risk reduction (e.g., 100% green with no negative tests).

title: Validation suite itself is wrong or vacuous
description: Tests pass trivially (assertions never fail, mocked sources), so controls appear validated.

title: Auditor declines to rely on agent-produced or agent-collected evidence
description: CPA firm requires manual reperformance, eroding the cost model of automated assurance.

title: AI provider treated as undisclosed subservice organization
description: AI provider used in in-scope processes is not addressed in the system description/CSOCs, creating a report qualification risk.

title: Unbounded agent cost or resource consumption
description: Runaway loops or adversarial inputs drive inference spend or exhaust quotas, degrading other controls.

title: Inter-agent message spoofing or cascading error
description: One agent's corrupted output is accepted by another as trusted instruction, propagating errors across mappings, remediations and reports.

title: Confidential prompts and traces retained beyond need
description: Agent traces containing personal or confidential data are retained in logs or provider systems longer than permitted.

title: Over-reliance on formal methods or tests as proof of effectiveness
description: Verified models or passing tests are presented as proof that deployed controls operate effectively, though they do not verify executable code or real operation.

title: Kill switch unavailable or untested
description: Emergency agent suspension depends on the same identity plane or tooling the agent can affect, or has never been exercised.

title: External-witness anchoring lapses unnoticed
description: Periodic anchoring of evidence-log digests to an external timestamp/transparency service stops, removing tamper-evidence for the gap.

title: Financial misstatement in sponsor fund accounting
description: Ledger, valuation or fee errors flow into sponsor financial statements

title: Grant or disbursement fraud
description: Fraudulent payees, payee bank change fraud, collusive approvals

title: Cross-tenant data exposure
description: A sponsor or partner sees another tenant's data

title: Account takeover of privileged user
description: Phishing or token theft yields production or financial access

title: Software supply-chain compromise
description: Malicious dependency or build tampering

title: GLBA/state-law status misclassified
description: Treating contested legal status as settled either way

title: SOC 1 expected but not available at sale
description: Sponsor auditors or banks require SOC 1 Type 2; absence blocks or delays deals or forces direct auditor testing

title: Bank partner rejects third-party risk posture
description: Bank TPRM due diligence fails; payments capability blocked

title: Insufficient segregation of duties in a very small team
description: One or two people cannot be independent of their own controls

title: Irreversible retention lock set wrongly
description: WORM retention period set before legal/contract periods known

title: Assurance repository exposure
description: Assurance design repository is public contrary to owner instruction; sensitive content could leak if added

title: Missed breach notification deadline
description: Contractual deadlines (hours) shorter than legal ones

title: Ransomware or destructive attack
description: Production and backups encrypted or deleted

title: Internal build costs exceed purchase costs
description: Engineering effort on assurance tooling exceeds platform subscription and delays product

title: Key-person dependency
description: Assurance and approvals depend on one person

title: IRC 4966 taxable distribution enabled by platform
description: Grant to ineligible recipient triggers sponsor excise tax
